title: Explore orchestrator integrations (OpenClaw/Gas Town) vs client emitters
description:
## Context
Nexus currently models repo-facing runtime clients (e.g., Claude/Codex/OpenCode) as emit targets. We discussed whether OpenClaw and Gas Town should be added as clients.

Observation: OpenClaw and Gas Town are orchestration layers/wrappers around underlying runtimes, not direct repo config consumers in the same sense as runtime CLIs. Treating them as first-class "clients" may blur boundaries and create API confusion.

## Problem
We need a clear architecture boundary so Nexus can support these ecosystems without overloading the meaning of "clients".

## Proposal to Investigate
Define two distinct extension surfaces:
1) Runtime Client Emitters
- Emit repo artifacts consumed directly by runtime CLIs (e.g., .claude, .codex, .opencode, MCP config).

2) Orchestrator Integrations
- Adapters/plugins that translate Nexus graph into orchestrator-specific conventions/workflows (e.g., OpenClaw skill sync/install hints, Gas Town agent/runtime presets, mailbox/task glue), without pretending they are runtime clients.

## Research Questions
- What artifacts/actions does OpenClaw need from Nexus to be useful (skills, managed sync, metadata, hooks)?
- What artifacts/actions does Gas Town need (agent presets, role files, workflow templates, issue/beads mapping)?
- Which integration points are repo-scoped vs global/user-scoped?
- Should orchestrator integrations run at build/emit time, activation time, or as explicit commands?
- How should state hash and cleanup apply to non-file side effects?

## Deliverable
- 1-page architecture note (or issue comment summary) with recommendation:
  - Keep "clients" for runtime consumers only.
  - Add "integrations" / "orchestrators" plugin surface if justified.
  - Migration/back-compat strategy if any naming changes are needed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Clear taxonomy documented: runtime client vs orchestrator integration.
- Decision recorded on whether OpenClaw/Gas Town become clients or integration plugins.
- If plugins are chosen, minimal interface draft exists (inputs/outputs/lifecycle/state/cleanup semantics).

## Priority / Timing
Low priority; revisit after core v2 client/plugin work is stable.

description:
## What

## Proposal

  - GitHub releases/tags/changelog deltas for upstream clients
  - Docs path/schema snapshots for known spec pages

- Optional AI summarizer step to classify changes (breaking/additive/editorial).

## Acceptance
- Reproducible watcher job runs in CI/cron.
- Drift creates actionable Beads tasks automatically.
- Human-readable report includes affected Nexus modules/tests/docs.

description:
Goal: allow per-project variables/env while keeping defaults in dotfiles.

Design:

title: First-class enable ergonomics for Claude commands/agents in mkRepo
description:
## What
Evaluate and implement first-class enable ergonomics for Claude commands/agents (and hooks/settings as appropriate) in mkRepo config.

## Current state
- Definitions exist in dotfiles via claude.commands / claude.agents / claude.hooks / claude.settings.
- Enabling currently routes through enable.clients.claude.files path lists.

## Goal
Reduce path-level friction by providing a higher-level enable API (e.g., named command/agent selectors) while preserving explicit file mapping internally.

## Acceptance
- Decision documented: keep path-level only OR add first-class selectors.
- If implemented: tests + docs for new enable shape and compatibility behavior.
notes: Sixth slice landed: extracted selector planning from runNexus into compile stage helper (src/compile/clientPaths.ts) with tests (test/clientPathsCompile.test.ts). runNexus now calls resolveEnabledClientPaths() so adapter invocation + explicit path merge policy is centralized and easier to pluginize. Suite green: 85 pass, 0 fail.

title: Spec audit: Claude Code repo artifacts (commands/hooks/agents/settings)
description:
## What
Perform an evidence-backed Claude Code spec audit for repo-scoped artifacts and close gap with Nexus emitters.

## Scope
- Confirm canonical Claude Code artifact paths and file formats from official docs/source.
- Define exact supported set in Nexus v2 (skills, commands, hooks, agents, settings fragments if supported).
- Implement/adjust emitter + cleanup + state hash coverage.
- Add golden tests and migration notes.

## Acceptance
- Spec matrix with citations to upstream docs.
- `nexus` emits only supported Claude Code artifact types/paths by default.
- Full tests passing with create/update/remove coverage.
notes:
Implemented dotfiles convenience: `claude.settings` -> `.claude/settings.json` (+ TDD test).
Docs evidence: Claude settings scopes show project settings live at `.claude/settings.json` and `.claude/settings.local.json` (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings). Hooks examples reference `.claude/hooks/...` (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks). Skills docs mention `.claude/commands/` behaves like skills and `.claude/skills/` location (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slash-commands). Subagents docs confirm `.claude/agents/` (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents).
Boss decision: stick with declarative; no imperative MCP-adding CLI in Nexus. Next: beads task for Claude settings (likely `.claude/settings.local.json` support or declarative settings defs).

title: v2: Client plugin system — make emitters standalone plugins
description:
## What
Refactor Nexus so clients (claude/mcp/codex/opencode/…) are plugins with a stable interface, and allow third parties to ship new clients.

## Scope
- Define plugin interface: resolve(config)->artifacts, emit(artifacts)->writes, markers, cleanup hooks
- Core ships built-in plugins (claude + mcp first); others can be external
- Nix + TS packaging story for plugins
- Compatibility policy + versioning

## Acceptance
- Can install/enable a plugin client without changing Nexus core
- Plugins participate in state hash + cleanup
- Golden tests for built-in plugins still pass
